samples.summary: Empty-deck early return skips the whole teardown, leaving a live text-box editor / crop session anchored to a slide that no longer exists
samples.evidence: `if (doc.slides.length === 0) return undefined;` returns *before* `exitImageCrop(false)` / `exitEditMode('cancel')` / `setCellSelection(null)` / `selection.clear()` (lines 1550-1553). So when the removal that vanished the current slide also empties the deck, `currentId` stays dangling AND the mounted text box stays in the overlay with `editingElementId` non-null, and `cropSession` stays installed (its document-level keydown capture handler included, see finishCropSession at 2514). `render()` then bails at line 1428/1430 so the canvas is blank while a fully interactive text box floats over it; a subsequent commit from that box targets the removed slide id and throws out of the store (`MemSlidesStore.requireSlideIndex`). The local thumbnail path blocks a deck wipe (thumbnail-panel.ts:301), but two peers deleting disjoint halves concurrently, or an undo that removes the last slide, reaches slides.length === 0. The teardown block should run for the empty-deck case too (only the cursor move has no target).

samples.summary: Heal clears selection ids but not the drill-in scope, so a group scope from the removed slide leaks onto the healed slide
samples.evidence: `Selection.clear()` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/selection.ts:93) only resets `ids`; `scope_` is untouched (`setScope` is the only reset). After a heal the editor is on a different slide while `selection.getScope()` still names group ids that only existed on the vanished slide. `repaintOverlay` feeds that scope into its member-outline / scope-aware lookups (editor.ts:1108) and `pickAtScope` will classify the user's next click as `{kind:'outside'}` until the caller resets scope — i.e. one click is spent recovering. `setCurrentSlide` has the same gap, so this is a consistency bug rather than a regression, but the heal is the one place with no user gesture to recover it.

samples.summary: Teardown condition (`editingElementId !== null`) does not match `exitEditMode`'s own guard (`editingTextBox === null` early-return), so a divergent state leaves the editor wedged in a phantom edit
samples.evidence: Line 1551 calls `exitEditMode('cancel')` when `this.editingElementId !== null`, but `exitEditMode` returns immediately when `this.editingTextBox === null` (line 4329-4330) without clearing `editingElementId`. If those two fields can ever diverge (text box failed to mount / already detached), the heal's guard fires, does nothing, and `editingElementId` stays non-null forever — which permanently forces `render()` down the `forceRender(maskEditingElement(...))` branch (line 1442-1455), masking an element id that belongs to a deleted slide on every frame. Keying the heal off `editingTextBox`, or calling `finishEditMode()` directly, closes the mismatch.

samples.summary: Local delete-slide now emits a transient heal to the WRONG slide (plus an extra current-slide notification) between removeSlides() and setCurrentSlide()
samples.evidence: `store.batch(() => store.removeSlides([...targetIds]))` notifies synchronously, and SlidesView's listener calls `editor.markDirty(); editor.render();` in the same tick (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1051-1053). With the new heal, that render moves the cursor to the slide *before* the deleted one and fires `currentSlideListeners` (→ `broadcast()`/presence, thumbnail highlight) before line 321-322 sets the intended survivor (the slide *after* the anchor). Net result is a double notification and one frame painted on the wrong slide; it also means the crop session is discarded by the heal (`exitImageCrop(false)`) instead of going through `setCurrentSlide`'s `exitImageCrop(true)`. Moving `setCurrentSlide` inside/immediately around the batch, or computing the survivor before notifying, avoids the transient.

samples.summary: Heal tears down crop/text edit but not in-flight pointer gestures, whose captured slideId then commits to the removed slide
samples.evidence: The heal clears the selection while document-level gesture handlers stay installed. `startTableEdgeResize` captured `slideId = this.currentSlide()?.id` at pointerdown and commits on pointerup via `store.updateTableColumnWidths(slideId, ...)` (editor.ts:4476/4486) — after the heal that slide is gone, so the store throws out of a document `pointerup` listener; `pendingTableResize`, `insertKind`/insert-drag and connector-drag state are likewise not reset. The throw path predates this change, but the heal is the new point that declares interaction state anchored to the removed slide as torn down, and it only covers crop + text edit.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is present verbatim: editor.ts:1533 `if (doc.slides.length === 0) return undefined;` returns before the teardown at 1550-1553 and before `currentId`/`currentIndex` are healed (1544-1545). Consequently, on an empty deck an active text edit stays mounted (editingElementId non-null, editingTextBox attached at 4170) and a crop session stays installed — the document-level capture keydown handler is only removed in finishCropSession (2514-2519), reachable solely via exitImageCrop, which the early return skips. Both render() (1427-1431) and repaintOverlay() (1069-1080) then bail on `!slide`, so an interactive text box floats over a blank canvas and the crop mode is wedged with a leaked global listener. The branch is reachable: YorkieSlidesStore.removeSlide/removeSlides (yorkie-slides-store.ts:798-816) has no minimum-deck guard so remote peers can empty the deck, and empty decks are an explicitly handled state elsewhere (presenter.ts:73/526, slides-detail.tsx:479). The local thumbnail guard (thumbnail-panel.ts:301) and the seed/undo-baseline in slides-view.tsx:644-648 only cover local paths, so no `already-guarded` refutation holds. One sub-claim is wrong — a later commit does not escape the store because onCommit wraps the batch in try/catch (4121-4162) — but the stale interaction state, dangling currentId, and leaked listener remain a real correctness/invariant defect in this lens.
